questions.prompt: The soldier praises both the general and the sword; the latter defends the body, the former the state.
questions.answer: Mīles et ducem et gladium laudat; hīc corpus, ille cīvitātem dēfendit.

questions.prompt: Themistocles sent a letter to the king in the following words.
questions.answer: Themistoclēs hīs verbīs epistulam ad rēgem mīsit.

questions.prompt: The famous Solon, wisest of all, gave just laws to the citizens.
questions.answer: Solōn ille, sapientissimus omnium, iūstās lēgēs cīvibus dedit.

questions.prompt: That fellow, seized by greed, betrayed his own friends.
questions.answer: Iste homō, avāritiā captus, amīcōs suōs prōdidit.

questions.prompt: We praise the man who saved the besieged city.
questions.answer: Eum virum laudāmus quī urbem obsessam servāvit.

questions.prompt: I am not such a man as to be easily frightened by dangers.
questions.answer: Nōn is sum quī perīculīs facile terrear.

questions.prompt: This is virtue, not to abandon one's country in danger.
questions.answer: Haec est virtūs, patriam in perīculō nōn dēserere.

questions.prompt: I admire Cicero and Cato; the latter was stern, the former eloquent.
questions.answer: Cicerōnem et Catōnem admīror; hīc sevērus, ille disertus fuit.

questions.prompt: The famous Hannibal, leader of the Carthaginians, crossed the Alps with his army.
questions.answer: Hannibal ille, dux Poenōrum, Alpēs cum exercitū superāvit.

questions.prompt: We will give rewards to those who bravely drove back the enemy.
questions.answer: Eīs praemia dabimus quī hostēs fortiter reppulērunt.

questions.prompt: The king gave the envoys the following orders: that they surrender the city without delay.
questions.answer: Rēx lēgātīs haec mandāta dedit: urbem sine morā trāderent.

questions.prompt: Our forces are not such as to withstand so great an enemy.
questions.answer: Nōn eae sunt cōpiae nostrae quae tantum hostem sustineant.

questions.prompt: I often read Virgil and Horace; the latter wrote shorter poems, the former greater ones.
questions.answer: Vergilium et Horātium saepe legō; hīc breviōra, ille maiōra carmina scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: This is wisdom, to yield to the occasion and to control one's anger.
questions.answer: Ea est sapientia, temporī cēdere et īram regere.

questions.prompt: He was not the sort of man to abandon a friend in adversity.
questions.answer: Is nōn erat quī amīcum in rēbus adversīs relinqueret.

questions.prompt: Remember this, that no one attains glory without toil.
questions.answer: Illud memoriā tenēte, nēminem sine labōre glōriam adipīscī.

questions.prompt: The famous Alexander the Great subdued the whole world by arms.
questions.answer: Alexander ille Magnus tōtum orbem armīs subēgit.

questions.prompt: Peace and war are set before the state; the latter brings ruin, the former safety.
questions.answer: Pāx et bellum cīvitātī prōpōnuntur; hoc ruīnam, illa salūtem affert.

questions.prompt: I consider those citizens happy who obey the laws.
questions.answer: Eōs cīvēs beātōs habeō quī lēgibus pārent.

questions.prompt: The orator spoke in the following manner: that no one sins unpunished.
questions.answer: Ōrātor hunc in modum locūtus est: nēminem impūne peccāre.

questions.prompt: My ability is not such that I can bear so great a burden.
questions.answer: Nōn ea est facultās mea ut tantum onus sustineam.
